# Threat model

## What this project does and where untrusted input enters
- xavier: Rust memory runtime for AI agents (HTTP REST API, MCP server, CLI, P2P mesh between nodes, chat gateways) with SQLite-backed vector stores, at-rest encryption and a TypeScript panel-ui
- Untrusted input enters via:
  - HTTP REST API on :8006 (src/api, src/server: v1_api, auth_routes, pageindex, training, docbot routes); token, JWT and OAuth auth in src/auth2
  - MCP over HTTP/SSE (src/server/mcp) and MCP stdio (src/server/mcp_stdio.rs, 'xavier mcp')
  - P2P mesh peers (src/mesh, src/espacio/p2p.rs, NAT traversal in src/mesh/p2p): messages from other nodes are untrusted
  - Chat gateways (src/gateways: telegram_docbot, whatsapp; src/telegram)
  - Documents, repositories and archives ingested for indexing (src/documents, src/codebase, src/pageindex_glue)
  - panel-ui browser input served under :8006/panel
- Trusted (not treated as untrusted input):
  - The node operator, its configuration files and environment variables
  - Local SQLite stores written by the node itself

## Components that matter most / least
- Components that matter most:
  - src/auth2 and src/middleware (authentication and authorization)
  - src/api and src/server (HTTP and MCP surface)
  - src/mesh and src/espacio (peer-to-peer input, replication)
  - src/crypto, src/keystore, src/node_identity, src/secrets (key handling and at-rest encryption)
  - src/codebase and src/documents (parsing of untrusted content)
- Components that matter least / lower priority:
  - benches, examples, docs, installer, scripts (developer tooling)
  - panel-ui (TypeScript UI; scanned only as the HTTP client of the API)
- Auditor hotspots (KSM evidence, 0 finding(s) in 0 file(s); no code excerpts):
  - No auditor findings in scope.

## How to exercise it
- cargo build, then 'xavier http' with XAVIER_TOKEN set; readiness at GET /ready
- cargo test --lib for unit tests (hermetic subset runs offline)
- 'xavier mcp' starts the MCP stdio server

## How you rate severity
- auth bypass on the HTTP or MCP API: critical (human policy)
- denial of service from an authenticated client: medium (human policy)
- issues requiring a malicious local operator or config file: out of scope (human policy)
- memory corruption in unsafe code reachable from network input: critical (human policy)
- remote code or command execution from API, MCP, mesh or gateway input: critical (human policy)
